clue.text: Unfit bent and twisted?

definitions.meaning: someone unfit has let their body go and lacks condition
something bent and twisted has lost its proper form

explanation.surface: A wry description of a person in poor condition, as if their body had been warped.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase covers both poor physical fitness and an object deformed from its proper form.

clue.text: Highly decorated knight coming in to make a speech

indicators.note: the letter for knight comes in, placed inside the other word

parts.note: to orate is to make a formal speech
N is the chess notation for a knight

explanation.surface: A much-decorated knight arrives to deliver an address.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly decorated' suggests medals on the knight; it is the definition, meaning elaborately ornamented.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornate describes something elaborately adorned with ornament.

clue.text: Film best bowler, perhaps

parts.note: top means best, as in top marks
a bowler is an example of a hat

explanation.surface: The best bowler in a film, perhaps a cricketer.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Hat is the 1935 Fred Astaire and Ginger Rogers musical.
explanation.definitionFit: The name of a celebrated 1935 Astaire and Rogers dance musical.

clue.text: Second eleven winning after comprehensive instruction given by captain?

indicators.note: the remaining pieces follow, coming after the word for comprehensive

parts.note: full means comprehensive or complete
a team of eleven, as in cricket or football
a side that is winning is ahead

explanation.surface: A cricket second eleven wins after the captain's thorough team talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The sports captain is a red herring; the definition's captain is a ship's master ordering top speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's captain orders maximum speed forward with this command; the question mark flags the nautical sense.

clue.text: Pick up basket lying across hotel mat

parts.note: to pick up a sound is to hear it

indicators.note: the basket lies across the hotel letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a trug is a shallow gardener's basket
H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Collect a basket left lying over the hotel doormat.
explanation.definitionFit: A rug laid in front of the fireplace, a kind of mat.

clue.text: Tar, substance sealing top of carriageway

indicators.note: the substance seals the other letter in, surrounding it

parts.note: pith is the essential substance of something

indicators.note: in a down entry the top is the first letter

explanation.surface: Tar is the material used to seal the surface of a road.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitch is a black sticky tar-like substance from distillation.

clue.text: Employed American press chief

parts.note: the chief of a newspaper is its editor, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper editor from the United States is hired.
explanation.definitionFit: Something employed has been put to use, so the two past participles are synonyms.

clue.text: Quantity carried aboard a Polish destroyer, primarily at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so the letters are jumbled
primarily picks out the first letter

explanation.surface: A Polish warship sails with its cargo.
explanation.definitionFit: A shipload is the amount of goods a vessel carries.

clue.text: A high explosive, and yet I'm relaxed

indicators.note: relaxed means loosened, so the letters are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm even though handling a dangerous explosive.
explanation.definitionFit: Nobel's nitroglycerine-based blasting agent is a classic high explosive.

clue.text: Also fascinated by article on pub acquisition

parts.note: to be into something is to be keen on it
the is the definite article
a bar is a pub
a gain is something acquired

explanation.surface: Someone is also interested in a piece about buying a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means besides or in addition, as when something comes free with a purchase.

clue.text: The French female writer heading west for Asian republic

indicators.note: in an across entry, travelling west means running right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: LA is the feminine form of 'the' in French
a pen is a writing instrument

explanation.surface: A French woman author travels towards an Asian country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading west' turns LAPEN around to give the country.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan state between India and China is a federal republic in Asia.

clue.text: Heed military order

definitions.meaning: to pay heed is to take notice or care
the drill command telling soldiers to stand straight and still

explanation.surface: Obey the instruction barked on the parade ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Heed means careful notice, and the same word is the drill sergeant's command to stand to.

clue.text: Passage from 'North and South' included in feature

indicators.note: the compass letters are placed within the other word, as something included sits inside

parts.note: a trait is a distinguishing feature or characteristic
N is the compass abbreviation for north
S is the compass abbreviation for south

explanation.surface: An extract taken from the Gaskell novel North and South, featured somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North and South' looks like the title of Elizabeth Gaskell's novel; here it just supplies the compass letters N and S.
explanation.definitionFit: Transit is a journey or crossing from one place to another, the same as passage.

clue.text: Gangster in house, different mould

indicators.note: made different, the letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: A criminal lives in a house where a strange mould grows.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodlum is a violent criminal thug, particularly one in a gang.

clue.text: Candid talk in centre — listen with child outside

parts.note: the heart of something is its centre

indicators.note: the word for a small child is placed around the other piece, sitting on its outside

parts.note: a tot is a small child
to hear is to listen

explanation.surface: An honest conversation in a community centre: listen, with the child left outside.
explanation.definitionFit: A frank, intimate conversation in which both people speak openly and sincerely.

clue.text: Value placed on right club official

parts.note: to treasure is to value highly

explanation.surface: A club officer is valued and placed on the right.
explanation.definitionFit: The officer who looks after a club's funds and accounts.

clue.text: Spare the criminal, producing a list of his crimes?

indicators.note: criminal suggests something wrong, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: A plea for leniency to a crook with a long police record.
explanation.definitionFit: A police record of a person's arrests and convictions, in American slang.

clue.text: Sit astride rider's seat holding both ends of tether

indicators.note: the seat holds the other letters inside it

parts.note: a saddle is the seat a rider sits on

indicators.note: both ends means the first and last letters

explanation.surface: A rider sits on a horse tied by its tether.
explanation.definitionFit: To straddle is to sit with one leg on each side, astride something.

clue.text: Memorable song from Sam, yet Bogie's furious

indicators.note: furious suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Sam plays the famous song in Casablanca, though Humphrey Bogart's character is enraged.
explanation.walkthrough: Bogie was Humphrey Bogart's nickname; in Casablanca Sam the pianist plays this song, which Bogart's Rick had banned.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1931 standard, made famous by the film Casablanca, is one of the best-remembered songs in cinema.

clue.text: Quiet nursing home, very small

indicators.note: nursing means holding close, so the word for quiet holds the other inside

parts.note: mute means silent or quiet
to be in is to be at home

explanation.surface: A quiet nursing home that is tiny.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, stressed on the second syllable, means tiny.

clue.text: Agent put away copy

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative or agent
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: An agent is jailed, his copy stored.
explanation.definitionFit: To repeat an action or words is to copy or duplicate them.

clue.text: Broken spades on ground

parts.note: S is the card-suit abbreviation for spades
ground food has been crushed or mashed

explanation.surface: Garden spades lie broken on the earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Something smashed has been shattered into pieces, which is to say broken.

clue.text: Waste beginning to deter Arctic explorer

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: John Ross and his nephew James Clark Ross were polar explorers

explanation.surface: Rubbish starts to deter a polar explorer.
explanation.definitionFit: Dross is worthless scum or rubbish, waste matter.

clue.text: Use one, about to dish up outside

indicators.note: the serving word goes around the other letters, sitting on their outside

parts.note: to serve food is to dish it up
I is the Roman numeral for one
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Take one, about to serve food outdoors.
explanation.definitionFit: Service means use or employment, as in a car still in service or a coat giving good service.

clue.text: Aim always, it's said, to make an industrious effort

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the words are taken by how they sound

parts.note: an aim is an end, and always is ever, giving END EVER when spoken

explanation.surface: Advice to keep a goal in view forever and work hard.
explanation.definitionFit: An endeavour is an earnest, diligent attempt to achieve something.

clue.text: Entertain a goddess, one of nine

parts.note: the Muses were the nine Greek goddesses of the arts

explanation.surface: Host a goddess who is one of nine sisters.
explanation.definitionFit: To amuse is to divert or entertain someone so they are pleased.

clue.text: Over-sentimental message abridged

indicators.note: something abridged is cut short, so the final letter is removed

parts.note: a tweet is a short message posted online

explanation.surface: A shortened message turns out sickly sweet.
explanation.definitionFit: Twee means excessively sweet, quaint or sentimental.

clue.text: Scathing, series probing a hospital department

indicators.note: something probing pushes into another, so this word goes inside

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department
a string is a series, such as a string of wins

explanation.surface: A harsh series of inquiries into a hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Astringent remarks are sharp and severe, like scathing criticism.
